primitives.name: Spatial Graph Representation
primitives.verbatim_quote: To investigate this, we generate graphbased representations connecting players, which serve as input for a Graph Convolutional Network (GCN) for the subsequent classification of these graph structures.
primitives.latex: $G = (V,E)$, where $V$ represents players and $E$ encodes pairwise relative positions and interactions.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'G': 'Graph structure', 'V': 'Set of players (dimensionless)', 'E': 'Edge set representing interactions (dimensionless)'}
primitives.assumptions: Static graph assumption; Euclidean distance threshold defines adjacency; player roles are fixed.
primitives.breakdown_regime: High-dimensional feature space ($>10^3$) causes overfitting; sparse graphs ($|E| \ll |V|^2$) reduce expressiveness.

layer2.mapping: GSI: Convert graph nodes to probabilistic events; GSE: Encode state transitions via edge flows.
layer2.telemetry: Average edge count per frame, node degree distribution

primitives.name: Graph Convolutional Network
primitives.verbatim_quote: To investigate this, we generate graphbased representations connecting players, which serve as input for a Graph Convolutional Network (GCN) for the subsequent classification of these graph structures.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'H^{(l)}': 'Node feature matrix at layer $l$ (dimensionless)', '\\tilde{A}': 'Normalized adjacency matrix (dimensionless)', 'W^{(l)}': 'Weight matrix (learned)', '\\sigma': 'Activation function (dimensionless)'}
primitives.assumptions: Local homophily assumption; graph Laplacian is diagonalizable; batch normalization stabilizes gradients.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Vanishing/exploding gradients for deep networks ($L > 10$); adversarial perturbations on edges cause misclassification.

layer2.mapping: GSI: Message passing corresponds to belief propagation; GSE: Transition matrices are learned from graph flows.
layer2.telemetry: Classification accuracy, computational complexity per forward pass

primitives.name: Binary Classification
primitives.verbatim_quote: This study addresses the classification of offensive plays in the National Football League (NFL) as either pass or rush, utilizing official NFL datasets from 2022-2023 season.
primitives.latex: y \in \{0,1\}$ for rush and pass respectively.
primitives.assumptions: Balanced dataset; linear separability in high-dimensional space; zero-sum game between offense and defense.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Class imbalance ($>2:1$) degrades F1-score; noisy features cause overconfident predictions.

layer2.mapping: GSI: Bayes-optimal classifier maps posterior odds to decisions; GSE: State-value functions estimate expected payoffs.
layer2.telemetry: Precision-recall curve, receiver operating characteristic (ROC) area
